sections.title: The letter a
paragraphs: The letter is named (a) /a/. It has one sound. You hear it in the word (agua) /ˈa.ɣwa/, which means water. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. This vowel stays clear and steady in every word.

sections.title: How to say a
paragraphs: Open your mouth wide and let your jaw drop comfortably. Keep your tongue flat and low in the central part of your mouth. Do not push your tongue forward or pull it back. Touch your throat with your hand. You feel your vocal cords shake as you make this sound.

sections.title: Spelling and sounds
paragraphs: This letter always makes the same sound in all positions. You hear this sound at the start, in the middle, and at the end of a word. Listen to this sound in (casa) /ˈka.sa/ and (madre) /ˈma.dɾe/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not turn this letter into a weak schwa. A schwa is a short, weak vowel in the middle of the mouth, like the a in about. Do not pronounce this letter like the vowel in cat. Keep your mouth open wide and keep the sound steady until the end.
